Edoran’s Sealed Note — recovered from Z4 (Scene 1)

The note Z4 tries to burn at the NE lantern post in round 2. Hand to players if recovered. If burned, describe the smell of singed wax and old paper. The content surfaces through other routes — Jaret knows it, Theron has seen the handwriting before.

[A single sheet of paper, rolled and sealed with dark red wax. The seal is a circle with a small sun-ring pressed into the center — the mark of the Auris Wounded faction. The paper inside is dry, precise, written with the care of someone who knows this document will be read by strangers.]

The willing heart gives freely what the bound heart cannot.
You were hired to investigate. You will find the truth. When you do — ask yourself who benefits from your finding it, and whether those people were willing.
This is not a threat. It is the only question that matters.

[No signature. The handwriting is formal Auris liturgical script — the kind learned in a seminary, not a counting house.]

Religion DC 10 or History DC 10: liturgical Auris script — formal, seminary-trained. DC 14: specifically the Wounded faction’s grief liturgy, not standard Auris worship. The Wounded faction believes the Dawnborn’s deaths would be meaningful. The author is clergy, or former clergy.
Theron Waide, if shown this note, goes very still. He has seen this handwriting before — earlier correspondence, same hand, same style. “Someone has been writing to me about this for years. Arguing that the anchor holders must choose freely.” He did not know who. He filed it.
If the note burned: Jaret, at the Dawnhall approach, will mention that “Brother Edoran keeps that scripture close — says it to anyone who asks why the Restorers won’t force the issue.” That’s the recovery path.




Archive Door Riddle — carved into the restricted stacks door (Scene 2)

Carved directly into the door face in Corven’s private notation — unreadable without the Notation Key. If players have assembled Fragments 1+2+3 (Sessions 1-2), they can decode it. Otherwise they must solve the riddle from the meaning-context alone, or wait for Theron.

[The restricted door of the Varenhold Civic Archive’s third floor. Stone, solid, cold. Carved into its face: rows of small symbols in Corven’s private cipher. Directly below the cipher, in plain script added by a different hand, at some later date:]

“In case the cipher proves too much — the question is plain enough once you see it.”

[Below that, in plain language, the same riddle the cipher encodes:]


I am given only when no one compels it.
Forced, I become something else entirely.
I am the difference between a gift and a theft.
What word names the thing that makes the difference?


Answer: CONSENT. Spoken aloud at the door, in any form. The door responds to the word and its synonyms.
Wrong (first attempt): low resonance tone, audible from the floor below. Theron appears at the landing, coat askew, ink on sleeve. He looks at the door. He looks at the players. He says nothing immediately.
Wrong (third attempt): tone sharpens, thin crack of light along the door frame. Door won’t respond for one hour. Theron: “Perhaps I should show you what I know before you try again.” He becomes the guide.
The riddle is the campaign’s central word. Players who solve it before Theron intervenes are already asking the right question. The small script addition (“in case the cipher proves too much”) is in Theron’s handwriting. He wanted someone to open it. He could not open it himself.




Dawnmark Star Chart — east wall of restricted stacks (Scene 3)

Full chart, permanently mounted, labeled in Common script. Show to players when they examine the east wall of the restricted stacks. This contains everything needed to solve the star-wheel puzzle.

[A large paper chart, mounted in a wide wooden frame, covering most of the east wall. Stars labeled in plain Common. One constellation is circled in red ink — recent addition, not original to the chart. A note below it reads: “overhead on the night of the ritual, Year 48.”]
╔══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╗
║  VARENHOLD OBSERVATORY — NIGHT SKY REFERENCE                     ║
║  Year 48, Third Month. The Dawnmark Constellation (circled).     ║
╠══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╣
║                                                                  ║
║  WEST ──────────────────────────────────────────────── EAST      ║
║  (rises first)                                   (rises last)    ║
║                                                                  ║
║                                                                  ║
║       ★                    ★                         ★           ║
║    VAEL'S               SHEPHERD'S                TRAILING       ║
║    CROWN                  EYE                      LIGHT         ║
║  [leftmost]            [middle]                  [rightmost]     ║
║  [anchor pt]           [pivot]                   [brightest]     ║
║                                                                  ║
║  ╔══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╗     ║
║  ║          ← THE DAWNMARK CONSTELLATION →                 ║     ║
║  ║  West-to-east rise order: Crown, Eye, Trailing Light.   ║     ║
║  ║  The Dawnmark was directly overhead at 02:14, Year 48.  ║     ║
║  ╚══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╝     ║
║                                                                  ║
║  [Dozens of other constellations labeled across the chart —      ║
║   only the Dawnmark is circled in red.]                          ║
╚══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╝

Star-wheel solution: Ring 1 = Vael’s Crown. Ring 2 = Shepherd’s Eye. Ring 3 = Trailing Light. West-to-east rise order. The chart provides this in plain language — no roll required to read it. DC 12 Arcana or Investigation confirms the reading and gives the order explicitly.
Wrong configuration: shelves physically rotate. 30 minutes lost, one level of exhaustion on the operator. After two wrong attempts: distant footsteps on the floor below.
Partial success (two of three rings correct): shelf 4-17-1 and 4-17-2 open but not 4-17-3. Players can see the correct shelf is one ring setting away.
The red circle ink is Theron’s. He circled it when he started to understand. He never set the rings. He could not bring himself to.




Corven’s Public Notes — found in shelf 4-17-3 (Scene 3)

The outer folder on shelf 4-17-3. Hand to players when they open the correct shelf. This is Corven’s formal record — the version he was willing to have found. Fragment 1 is tucked inside (see next card).

[Several pages of dense formal notation, bound with a dark cord. The cover page bears the Archive’s filing stamp: “Ritual of Eternal Dawn — Technical Documentation — Archmagister A. Corven.” Filed Year 48. Not opened since.]

RITUAL OF ETERNAL DAWN — TECHNICAL SUMMARY Archmagister A. Corven — Filed for Archive Record
The mechanism employed in the Year 48 ritual attempt draws on distributed sympathetic resonance — a configuration in which the anchor points for the ritual’s energy are distributed across multiple sites rather than concentrated at a central point.
This approach was chosen specifically because concentrated application at a single anchor risks cascade failure. The distributed model is more stable under load, though it requires precise calibration across all points simultaneously.
The living conduit mechanism was selected as the most reliable method for maintaining the distributed sympathetic anchors over time. Theoretical alternatives were considered and rejected.
The ritual did not fail in the manner first reported.
Further details are encoded in the supplementary notation. The key to that notation is provided separately, in three portions.
[The document ends here. The next several pages are dense notation — unreadable without the Notation Key.]

“Distributed sympathetic anchors” and “living conduit mechanism” are the two phrases players cannot fully decode yet. They have the language. They do not have the referents. That lands in Session 2.
“The ritual did not fail in the manner first reported” — Corven knew what actually happened. He filed this document in plain language and then made the explanation unreadable without a key he split into three fragments. He was protecting something and creating a path to it at the same time.
“Living conduit mechanism” = the Dawnborn. Players will understand this when Theron says “extinguished” in Session 2. Until then, the phrase sits in their notes.




Fragment 1 — Corven’s Private Notation Key (found in shelf 4-17-3)

Tucked inside the Corven’s Public Notes folder. A single sheet, well-preserved. Hand to players when they examine shelf 4-17-3’s contents. This is one of three fragments — alone it is partial. With Fragment 2 (Session 2, Resonance Box) and Fragment 3 (Session 3, workroom), the full cipher is readable.

[A single sheet of paper in a careful, precise hand. At the top: “Notation Reference — Section I of III.” Along the right edge, the grid clearly continues but the page stops. This is deliberately incomplete.]
╔══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╗
║  CORVEN PRIVATE NOTATION — FRAGMENT I OF III                  ║
║  Section I: Base Symbols (partial — see Sections II, III)     ║
╠══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╣
║                                                              ║
║   ✦ = T     ◈ = E     ⬡ = N     ⬟ = L     ⬠ = I            ║
║   ◆ = G     ◇ = H     ○ = B     ● = R     ◎ = S            ║
║                                                              ║
║   [continues →] Section II carries: ⊕ ⊗ ⊙ △ ▽ ▲ ▼ □ ■ ▪ ▸ ║
║   [continues →] Section III carries: remaining symbols        ║
║                                                              ║
╠══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╣
║                                                              ║
║  TWO PLAIN-LANGUAGE NOTES (in Corven's hand):                ║
║                                                              ║
║  Note 1:                                                     ║
║  "The weight borne willingly is not the same weight as the   ║
║   weight imposed. This is not a philosophical observation.   ║
║   It is an engineering specification."                       ║
║                                                              ║
║  Note 2:                                                     ║
║  "The mechanism will not function as designed if the         ║
║   distinction is collapsed."                                 ║
║                                                              ║
╚══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╝

Players can use the 10 symbols in Fragment I to decode any text that only uses those letters (T, E, N, L, I, G, H, B, R, S). Most of Corven’s encoded text uses the full cipher — partial decoding yields fragments with gaps.
The two plain-language notes are the most important content on the page. “Engineering specification” is Corven saying: consent is not a value judgment embedded in the ritual — it is a mechanical requirement. The ritual fails if consent is absent. This is the seed that becomes the Inversion pathway.
Fragment 2 is in the Resonance Box (Session 2). Fragment 3 is in Isolde’s workroom notes (Session 3).




Restorer Pamphlet — handed out near the Dawnhall (Scene 4)

Jaret hands one of these to whoever seems most receptive as players approach the Dawnhall. Jaret will answer questions honestly if asked directly.

ON THE NATURE OF THE LIGHT WE HAVE BORROWED A Philosophical Address from the Society for Ritual Restoration
The sun did not leave us by accident.
It was held — anchored against its nature, bound by mechanisms our predecessors understood imperfectly and executed without the consent of those most affected.
We do not blame the architects of Year 48. They acted in fear, in haste, for reasons that seemed sufficient at the time. We do not seek punishment. We seek resolution.
The amber light sustains us. We acknowledge this. But sustainability built on a foundation that was never chosen freely is not a gift. It is a debt. And debts, left unpaid, accumulate.
We are not Restorers because we wish destruction. We are Restorers because we understand that some things cannot hold forever — and it is more merciful to choose the moment than to wait until the moment chooses for us.
If you have questions, Jaret will answer them honestly.
— The Society for Ritual Restoration, Year 98

What the pamphlet does not say: the mechanism requires the death of the ten Dawnborn.
Jaret knows this. The pamphlet doesn’t say it. If players ask Jaret directly what “resolution” means, he pauses — then tells the truth. He is not a liar. He leads with the argument before the cost.
Players who came through session 0.5 already know Restorers exist and have operational capacity. What’s new here: this is a different chapter’s public-facing theology. The vault beneath the Dawnhall was the Restorers’ practical work. This pamphlet is their argument. They are not the same.







Pel — The Recognition [Frank’s player only]

Play when Sera Voss first looks at Pel directly — whether or not Pel has said anything.

She’s been talking to the group. Giving clear, complete answers the way she always gives them — which you noticed immediately, because you have never once in your professional life received a complete answer from someone in authority.
She turns to you specifically. Not because you said anything. Because she looked at the group and then looked at you twice.
Then she says your name.
Not “you” or “the investigator” or “your colleague.” Your name. First name. The one you stopped using when you started working criminal investigation, because it was safer to be a title than a person.
She remembers your name. You were a stranger in a burning building. You were unconscious for part of it. She didn’t know you then and she doesn’t know who you are now.
She says: “I thought it might be you. When the Chancellor mentioned investigators, I thought — the probability of it was low. But.”
She doesn’t finish that sentence.
What do you do?



Serah — Divine Sense Reading [Kirsten’s player only]

Play when Serah uses Divine Sense in the Dawnhall.

You’ve used Divine Sense in the Chancellor’s study: nothing. In the Archive: nothing. Standard Spire Quarter. Bureaucratic and unglamorous and theologically unremarkable.
The Dawnhall is different.
No celestials. No fiends. No undead. Those are the categories your training gave you — the things it names, the presences it identifies. What you’re feeling doesn’t fit any of them.
Sera Voss is standing twelve feet away explaining the Dawnhall’s intake procedures to the rest of the group. She is not radiating anything dangerous or holy or corrupt.
She is radiating presence. Like standing near a hearth where the fire hasn’t been lit yet. The stone is warm. Something is about to burn. It isn’t burning now.
You have felt this once before — standing at a wayshrine, very young, in the rain. The Wanderer’s shrines feel like that. Like something absent that is still somehow there.
Sera Voss is not a wayshrine.
You don’t know what she is. Write it down somewhere. You will need to remember this feeling later.



Keothi — The Seeds [Dennis’s player only]

Play when Keothi is in the Dawnhall kitchen or offers the seeds to anyone.

The cook’s name is Mira. Not the Chancellor — a different Mira. She’s been in this kitchen for nine years, since the last head cook left and nobody qualified came to replace her, so she stayed.
She hands you a wooden spoon while you’re standing near the prep area. Not a question. Not an invitation. Just: here, you look like you know what to do with this. You do.
She tells you, while you work, that they get two flour deliveries a month and one root vegetable shipment from a farm in the northern district that is on its last good season. She says this the way farmers say things — without drama, because the numbers are the drama.
You have the seeds in your pack.
You brought them for the city. For the Chancellor, or whoever represents the city officially. You brought them as a gift.
Looking at this kitchen — at Mira’s hands, at the careful rationing on the prep table, at the single small window that looks out on amber light and no soil — you understand that the city isn’t the Chancellor.
What do you do with the seeds?

title: 24  Session 2 — The Living Conduit
text:
Level 5 · ~3 hours · RP / Puzzle / Revelation / Tension
“When you know someone will die for a cause — do you tell them before they choose, or after?”



📋 Quick-Reference Card

Central Question: Do you have the right to decide someone else’s fate, even to save thousands?
Session Arc: Care → Understand → Shatter → Choose









NPC
Want
Fear
Lie




Sera Voss
To be useful while she still can
That she’s already past the threshold of return
“I’m not afraid of what the ritual means”


Theron Waide
Absolution
That telling the truth will destroy the thing it’s trying to save
“I found out recently”


Harran Lecht
The ritual stopped — by any means
That the Dawnborn have already chosen
“We only want to talk”



Handouts this session: - Fragment II (Scene 2) — brass puzzle cylinder, Dawnmark star map - Partial decoding sheet (Scene 3) — two-column cipher, incomplete without Fragment I
Key beats: 1. Sera has been investigating independently — players realise she’s further along than they expected (Scene 1) 2. The Resonance Box opens: three rings (two runic, one lunar/solar) yield Fragment II — second partial win (Scene 2) 3. “SENTIENT NODES” decoded — the Dawnborn are the anchors; main cipher now almost fully readable (Scene 3) 4. Theron confesses eleven years of silence (Scene 4) 5. The Pale Gathering manifests — what the box released; Harran arrives at the worst possible moment (Scene 5)





📁 Setup



📄 Story So Far

Session 1 ended inside the Varenhold Archive. Players solved the access puzzle (the Fragment I cylinder), decoded Corven’s original research, and left before Harran Lecht’s contact arrived. Players have already met and interacted with Sera Voss — she is not a stranger. The relationship is warm but unresolved. Sera is not yet sure what the players represent: help, complication, or both.
Edoran is dead. Players killed him during or after the Restorer ambush. He was underwhelming — a man who had been carrying something too long without learning to fight. On his body: a sealed note in Auris scripture (“The willing heart gives freely what the bound heart cannot”) and a second scrap, apparently never delivered: “You have no idea what you are looking for. When you find it, you will understand why I did not want you to.” The Restorer faction exists without a leader. They are scrambling. Someone will fill that space. Players don’t know who yet.
Fragment I is a brass cylinder etched with partial cipher symbols. First partial win (already earned): the self-cipher on Fragment I decodes to “THE LIGHT IS STILL THERE” — the sun is not gone, only blocked. This shifts the question from how do we make a new sun to how do we unblock the one that remains. The main ritual cipher is partially legible with Fragment I alone: “SUN RETURNS” and “_ILLING RELE_SE” surface, but the mechanism is still incomplete. A second fragment is needed to read most of the rest.
What players carry into this session: Fragment I (already partially decoded). Edoran’s two notes. The knowledge that someone organised enough to intercept them on day one is gone — and whatever that means for who comes next. And a relationship with Sera that has been started but not finished.



📄 Current Player State


Location: Lowmark district, Varenhold. Evening light (amber, always amber). Markets winding down.
Mood: Cautious curiosity, edged with something harder. They killed a faction leader they barely understood. They have a physical object they can’t decode and a name from the Chancellor — a face they haven’t seen.
Resources: Full spell slots (long rest between sessions). Fragment I in hand.
Information gap: They know the ritual exists. They do not know the Dawnborn are its anchors.

(Passive Perception ≥ 13: The streets thin out faster than normal for this hour. People glance up at the amber sky and move inside. This happens every evening in Varenhold — a reflex fifty years old.)



📄 The Truth — What This Session Reveals

The revelation: The Dawn Ritual does not use energy drawn from ley lines, Spire capacitors, or stored ambient magic. It uses people. Specifically: the Dawnborn — survivors of the original Silence — whose bodies adapted to fill the gap the sun left. The ritual reactivates the sun by draining that adaptation permanently. Every Dawnborn who survives the ritual is left as an ordinary person in a world that no longer has the disease they were immune to. Every Dawnborn who doesn’t survive the ritual is ash.
The escalation of stakes:







Scale
Stakes




Personal
Sera Voss — warm, alive, specific — will probably die in the ritual


Local
All 14 known Dawnborn in Varenhold face the same choice


Faction
The Reckoning wants to force the ritual regardless of Dawnborn consent


Cosmic
Without the ritual, the grey sickness kills 60% of Varenhold within four years



Pre-session secrets (ask each player privately before starting):

One player: “Your character has noticed Sera in the Dawnhall before. They don’t know her name. What did they notice about her?”
One player: “Your character has a family member who died of grey sickness. How recent is that loss?”
One player: “Your character read something in the Archive about the Silence — what single detail stuck with them?”

These are seeds. They don’t change the plot. They make the revelation personal.



📄 Session Map

Scene 1 (RP)       → Sera summons players — she's been investigating. They compare notes.
Scene 2 (Puzzle)   → The Resonance Box: 3 rings (Gebo/Dagaz/Full Sun). Fragment II retrieved.
Scene 3 (Reveal)   → "SENTIENT NODES." The decoding. Main cipher nearly complete — one symbol missing.
Scene 4 (RP)       → Theron's confession. Eleven years. Silence in the room.
Scene 5 (Combat)   → The Pale Gathering: spirits released by the box, Harran arrives mid-crisis.
If players skip Scene 1 (refuse to meet Sera, go straight to Theron): Run Scene 4 first. Theron’s confession hits harder without the emotional investment — but players who chose not to meet Sera will feel the cost of that choice when they do meet her in Session 3.
If players stall in Scene 2 (puzzle takes too long): Sera can offer to “show them a trick her father taught her” — she’s seen the box before. She sets two cylinders; players solve the remaining three. She doesn’t know what it opens or why it matters.
If players try to skip to Theron after Scene 3 (bypass Scene 4): Theron finds them. He’s been watching the Archive for anyone who touched the box. His confession scene works in any location.





📁 Scene 1 — Sera Voss: A Conversation Already Started (RP)



📄 Quick Card








Goal
Deepen the relationship — players realise Sera has been investigating independently and is further along than they knew


Location
Dawnhall common room, Lowmark district


Beat 2
Sera confirms one of the other Dawnborn — Aldric — has gone quiet. Not taken. Just disappeared from sight. She’s already worked out what that means.


Exit
Runner delivers Theron’s message: “She has the box.”


DC
Insight DC 13 (Sera is managing fear, not reporting it); Investigation DC 11 (Reckoning pamphlet found under side door — different paper stock, recent print)


Secondary Objective
Listen before speaking. Players who immediately tell Sera what they found in the Archive miss three things she’s already pieced together. Let her go first — she’s been working this longer.






📄 Read Aloud — Arrival


The Dawnhall is the same as you left it. Long and low, ceiling brown from decades of burning, the sound of tired people and scraping spoons. But she is watching the door. She sees you before you’re through it — doesn’t stand, doesn’t call out — just pulls out the chair across from her before you’ve crossed the room. The recognition is there, but something else is under it. The specific stillness of someone managing a situation they haven’t told anyone about yet.
“Sit down.” She slides a folded pamphlet across the table without looking at it. Reckoning print — block lettering, promises of restoration, standard. “That was under the side door this morning. Not the public entrance. The side door.” A pause. “They know where I sleep.”
She pushes the half-eaten bowl toward the centre of the table out of habit. The broth is barely warm. She forgot she’d offered it.
“I wasn’t going to send for you. And then I decided I was.”

(Passive Perception ≥ 13: Two people have been watching you since you sat down. Dawnhall workers — not Reckoning. They’re watching Sera’s back. She didn’t ask them to. They decided.)
(Passive Insight ≥ 12: She’s already run through several versions of this conversation. She’s on the one she thinks you can use.)



📄 Scene Description

Sera Voss manages the Dawnhall’s emergency feeding programme. She has been doing this for nine years. She is not dramatic about it. She does not want credit. She wants the numbers to add up.
She was born in Varenhold three years before the Silence. She is one of fourteen known Dawnborn in the city. She doesn’t talk about that unless pressed, and even then she talks about it the way she talks about being left-handed: a fact, not an identity.
What’s changed since Session 1: She has been paying attention. She’s catalogued three new things: the Reckoning pamphlet under the side door, a terse message from Aldric (another Dawnborn) saying he “needs some time alone” — which he has never said in nine years — and a feeling she doesn’t have a name for. She has not connected all of these out loud yet. She is waiting to see what the players bring before she does.
What she wants right now: To compare notes with people who might know more than she does.
What she actually wants: For someone to tell her there is a way through this that doesn’t require anyone to die.
Voice: Flat, direct, occasionally dry. She does not perform warmth but she is warm. She offers food unprompted. She remembers names immediately.
DM Direction: Sera is further along in her own investigation than players expect. She’s not waiting to be informed — she’s comparing notes. The scene lands when players realise she’s been working this independently the whole time.



📄 Character-Specific Knowledge








Character
What they notice




Cleric / Paladin
(Religion DC 12, auto if Auris-domain) The Auris penitent’s mark on Sera’s wrist — she’s checked it twice since you sat down. Whatever she’s decided, she’s measuring it against a vow.


Druid / Ranger
(Nature DC 10) Her skin has a faint luminescence in direct lamplight — not glow, more like light reflects differently off her than off other people. Classic Dawnborn marker. It’s slightly stronger than it was when you last saw her. Stress does that sometimes.


Rogue / any Streetwise
(Passive Perception ≥ 15) The two workers watching Sera’s back are different from last time. Younger. Better placed near the exits. She’s quietly upgraded who she trusts around her.


Fighter / Soldier background
(Auto) The pamphlet is folded so the print faces inward. Not embarrassment — she doesn’t want anyone else in the room to read the header. She’s been carrying it for hours and hasn’t shown anyone else.


History DC 14
The Dawnhall was originally the Archmagister’s residential wing. The placard at the door has been removed but the mounting bracket is still there. Whoever turned this into a feeding hall made a deliberate point of not commemorating who built it.






📄 Beat 2 — “One of the others isn’t answering.”

After players have shared something (or if they stay quiet, Sera decides to go first):

“Aldric.” She says the name like it costs something. “He’s been coming here every third day since we were children. Reliable as lamp oil. Five days ago he stopped.” She looks at the table. “I sent someone to his room. His coat is still there. His tools. He hasn’t gone on a trip.” A breath. “He’s just — gone quiet.”
“The Reckoning doesn’t kill Dawnborn. Not if they need us for something. So he’s not dead.” She looks up. “Which means someone convinced him to stop being visible. And the only thing that makes a Dawnborn suddenly invisible is fear.”
She flattens the Reckoning pamphlet on the table. “So. What did you find in the Archive?”

(Passive Insight ≥ 12: She already knows some of what they found. She’s not asking to be informed — she’s asking to see if they’ll be honest.)
DM Direction: Let players share what they know. Sera is not shaken by the revelation about the Dawnborn as ritual components — she’s already suspected something along these lines. What lands is the confirmation that someone organised is moving. The emotional beat: she’s been carrying this alone, and now she isn’t.



📄 Exit — Theron’s Message

A Dawnhall worker comes in with a folded note. Sera reads it, folds it again, and passes it to the nearest player without comment.
The note (in Theron’s handwriting): “She has the box. Corner of Ashfen Gate and the Unmarked Lane. The amber lamp with no hook. — W.”
Sera: “The Resonance Box. I’ve had it for eleven years. I thought it was decorative.” A long beat. “Apparently not.”
She stands up and picks up her coat. “Are we going now, or do you need to finish your soup?”
She accompanies the party to Scene 2 unless actively refused.





📁 Scene 2 — The Vault of the Resonance Box (Three Rooms)



📄 Quick Card








Goal
Reach the box through three layered defences; solve the runic combination; retrieve Fragment II


Location
Valdric’s Lockhouse, Ashfen Gate district — three nested rooms


Structure
Room 1: Entry/Surveillance (social/stealth); Room 2: Antechamber cipher lock (puzzle using F1); Room 3: The box itself (runic combination)


Beat 2
The box opens. Fragment II retrieved. Self-decode: “THE WILLING VESSEL IS THE MECHANISM.”


Second Partial Win
F1 + F2 together: lines 1, 2, 4, 5 of the ritual cipher become almost fully readable. Only “E_ACT” remains. The mechanism is clear. One symbol still missing.


Clock
If players were spotted in Room 1 — Reckoning backup arrives in 2d4 rounds from the moment they enter Room 2. Count openly.


Secondary Objective
Sera’s trust: how players treat the box signals who they are. The combination comes from reasoning, not forcing. Players who brute-force the rings get it open but Sera sees them do it — that gap costs trust in Session 3.







📄 Room 1 — The Lockhouse Entry



📄 Read Aloud


Valdric’s Lockhouse: a three-storey building of solid stone at the corner of Ashfen Gate and the Unmarked Lane. Amber lamp above the door — but no hook beneath it, exactly as Theron’s note said. The building is dark. It is not empty. A figure at the corner of the next block has been there since before you rounded the turn. Standing still, collar up, watching.

(Passive Perception ≥ 12: The figure has a crossbow slung low at their hip, kept out of the street light. They are not trying to be invisible — they are trying to be boring. Reckoning.)
(Passive Perception ≥ 15: A second figure on the roofline of the building opposite. They clocked you thirty seconds ago.)

The Challenge: The Reckoning has had this lockhouse under watch for at least two hours. They do not yet know about the box or its exact location — they are following Theron’s movements, not Sera’s. They will not stop players from entering (they have no grounds yet), but if players are visibly noted, they’ll signal their contact inside the hour.
Entry options:








Approach
DC / Condition
Consequence




Sera’s key (side entrance)
Auto — she has it
No alarm; Reckoning does not see who entered, only that the side door opened


Bluff / distract the watcher
Deception or Persuasion DC 13
Full pass; watcher doesn’t signal for 1 hour


Stealth (group check)
DC 14
Success: unseen. Failure: watcher makes a note — backup arrives later


Confront the watcher
Combat: CR 1 Scout; roofline watcher (CR 1/2 Scout) joins round 2
Loud. Watcher 2 signals before engaging — 4 rounds until 3 more Reckoning arrive



Sera: “I have a key. The side door. Let me go first.” She does not wait for agreement.




📄 Room 2 — The Antechamber (Cipher Lock)



📄 Read Aloud


The corridor behind the side entrance smells of old wood and the specific cold of a building that stores things rather than people. At the far end: a heavy iron door. Section C, according to the painted number. Sera’s section.
Her key does not fit. The lock has been changed.
A newer mechanism has been fitted — a rotating-ring cipher lock mounted over the original keyhole. Four brass rings, each engraved with ten symbols. You have seen these symbols before. You are holding one of the keys to reading them.

(Passive Perception ≥ 14: A thin wire runs from the back of the lock housing to a point three inches inside the door frame. Trigger mechanism. Whatever it activates is on the other side.)

The Lock: The Reckoning fitted this lock six hours ago. It is their own design — but they used the notation symbols as the ring characters, because the notation symbols were in their research files. They did not know that the very people coming here would already have Fragment I.
Mechanism: Four rings, each with 10 symbols from Fragment I. Setting them to spell a four-letter word in sequence. The correct word: ◎◇●⬠ = S, H, R, I… wait — that’s five letters. The correct word: ◎◇●⬠⬡◈ spells S-H-R-I-N-E (six). Actually the rings spell ◎◈⬠⬡ = S-E-I-N…
Correct reading: four rings, four symbols: - ✦◇●◈ = T · H · R · E → does not spell a word - Use ◎◈⬡✦ = S · E · N · T → “SENT” (the word on the original deposit slip Theron filed, visible if players search the room)
A deposit receipt pinned to the wall nearby (Perception DC 11 to notice): “Section C contents: three crates personal effects, one wrapped parcel — SENT for long-term hold. Depositor: Waide, T.” The word SENT is the access code.

📄 The Decoding Process



📄 Read Aloud — The Decoding


Nobody decides to move closer — they just are. Chairs pulled in, the lamp repositioned without discussion, coats left on because nobody is thinking about coats. The two cylinders interlocked are heavier than they should be. When you begin to rotate them together, the sound is brass-on-brass: soft, precise, patient.
The Dawnhall continues on the other side of the door. Someone laughs at something. Spoons. A chair dragging. Normal. Irrelevant. In here: the scratch of charcoal as someone marks down each symbol. The particular quiet of people who have stopped breathing normally.
The text surfaces slowly. Some symbols worn past reading. The core is clear. The word at the centre of it — conduit — sits in the mouth wrong before anyone says it aloud.


How it works: Fragment I is a key cylinder. Fragment II is the ciphertext. When interlocked and rotated to alignment, the symbols from both fragments combine to produce legible pre-Silence script. The script is the original ritual notation.
A player who attempts to decode gets the following (no check required — the mechanism is mechanical, not mental):

The combined cylinders, when rotated slowly, produce a sequence of symbols that correspond to the oldest known Varenhold writing system. The message is partial — some symbols worn past reading — but the core is clear.
“…the conduit is not stone or silver or stored potential. The conduit is awareness sustained against the dark. The Dawnborn are not witnesses to the Silence. They are its answer. Their adaptation is the bridge. The ritual completes what was interrupted — it draws through what learned to hold the gap. Each anchor gives what they became.”

Translation for players who ask: The ritual runs through the Dawnborn. Their post-Silence adaptation is the mechanism. They are not observers. They are components.
Theron walks in as they finish the last line.
(Passive Perception ≥ 14: He’s been waiting outside. He heard the box open from the street.)



📄 Theron’s Arrival


A man in a scholar’s coat — thin, somewhere between fifty and worn-past-sixty — steps in without knocking. The door brings a second of cold air with it, then closes. He smells of old paper and ink and the specific tiredness of a man who has been carrying something for eleven years without being able to put it down.
He looks at the cylinders first. Then Sera. Then you. That order tells you something.
“You understand what that means.”
Not a question. He has been saying that sentence to himself for a very long time.

DM Direction: Do not rush past this moment. Let it land. Give players a beat to look at Sera — who is reading the same text they just decoded, expression unreadable. Then move to Scene 4.

📄 Read Aloud — Theron Speaks


Theron sits without being invited. Coat stays on — the coat of a man who arrived from somewhere and hasn’t decided he’s staying. He looks at his hands on the table, not at any of you.
Outside the door, the Dawnhall continues: voices, the scrape of a chair, someone calling a name. It sounds very far away. The gap between that sound and this room is the distance between people who don’t know yet and people who do. In your mouth, without reason, the aftertaste of tea that went cold while everyone was reading.
“I have been the Archive’s senior historian for twenty-three years. I found the original ritual documentation eleven years ago, in a collection donated by a Spire scholar who did not understand what he was giving us.”

📄 DM Direction — Hold the Silence

Incorporeal Movement. As Pale Anchor above.

Tactics: Dawn-Shades prioritise heavy-armour targets (high STR scores drain faster). They do not go for Sera — they leave her for the Anchors. Any player who deals radiant damage becomes their next priority (eliminate the threat before it eliminates them). Morale: Do not flee. Do not pursue beyond 60 ft of the box.

Harran’s limit: Will not leave Sera until she is out of the building or the spirits are gone. He does not explain this. He will explain in Session 3, if anyone asks.




📊 Scaling Notes

If players are trivialising early (round 1 radiant nova eliminates half the shades): - Anchor Form triggers immediately on first Anchor reaching half HP — spawns 2 Shades instead of 1 - The second Pale Anchor uses Resonance Pull to claim both cylinders — it is not attacking, it is moving toward the cylinders. Players must physically block its path or pull the cylinders away.
If players are struggling badly (two characters at half HP by round 2): - Theron grabs the nearest lamp and smashes it on the floor in the centre of the shade cluster — improvised Luminous Burst: DC 10 CON save for all Shades in 10 ft radius, 2d8 fire/radiant on failure. He yells: “Bright light! Get light!” - Harran directs an Enforcer to cover the back exit — Sera can flee with a bonus action if she’s adjacent - Close the box option becomes obvious to Sera: she moves toward it on round 3 if nobody else does
Nonmagical weapon problem: Characters with no magical weapons, spells, or radiant effects cannot damage spirits at all. This is intentional for a gestalt party — it forces mixed tactical decision-making. The box combination, bright light, and the close-the-box option are all non-combat outs that do not require magic. A Fighter/Barbarian with no magic can still drag Sera to safety, close the box, or hold a chokepoint so the Wizard has time to cast.

A Dawnborn child (one of three known, under 12) chasing a ball into the street. She stops when she sees the players. She has the same faint luminescence as Sera. She’s old enough to know what it means and young enough to hate that she knows.

The Sealed Drawer order appears twice in Reckoning documents. They know it exists. They were told not to touch it. Someone who outranks Marsh gave that order.
The Chancellor’s seal appeared on Session 1 agents. These orders don’t carry her seal. The Reckoning’s command structure has a different source.

Status:  Stage 1 grey sickness, stable

         (matches VOSS, TOMAS reports)

Interview questions (approved list):
— Describe the sensation in your own words
— Does it feel like something is being held or like
   something is holding you?

Note: Subject does not know about the ward test.

PRIORITY: Commander needs subjective anchor experience
data before Phase 2. Extraction authorized if interview
impossible by standard methods.

Ward-emitter unit 3 deployed under kitchen floorboards.
Unit 4 deployed in linen storage. Both active.

The Reckoning is running multiple ward-emitters across the Dawnhalls. Session 1’s unit was one of four.
“Phase 2” is undefined. “Extraction” means they were prepared to take Petra by force.
They need the Dawnborn’s subjective experience of being a Lux Anchor. Why? That’s the question Session 3 answers.




Theron’s Journal — Day 4,017

Theron produces this himself at the Dawnhalls. He doesn’t hide it this time.

[A small leather journal, much-handled. Open to a recent entry. The handwriting is careful but tired.]

Day 4,017. Still counting. Still unable to tell them.
The mathematics of love and duty: I know the answer, and I cannot say it aloud. The day I found out — the day I should have gone to them immediately — I told myself I needed more time. That was 4,017 days ago.
What kind of scholar am I?
The Aldwyne family wrote again from Solenne. The younger son. He found my address somehow. He wanted to know if I had ever found what I was “close to understanding.” He doesn’t know what he’s asking. He doesn’t know that his father and sister are dead because I said I was close.
I did not write back.
I am still counting.


4,017 days = approximately 11 years.
Day 1 was an estate sale — the dispersal of Corven’s second assistant’s private papers. Theron attended. He bought the knowledge. He has been sitting on it since.
He is not a villain. He is someone who knew a terrible thing and found a thousand reasons, one per day, not to say it.




Edoran’s Letter — handed over at Scene 3 or found on Jaret (Session 1 carry-over)

If not already given in Session 1 — Edoran produces it himself when he finds the party.


The ritual’s completion is possible. The cost is real. I have been waiting eleven years for someone willing to face both without flinching. The Chancellor knows part of what I know. She chose not to finish the sentence. I will finish it.
I am not your enemy. I am not the Reckoning. The difference matters.
If you want answers rather than comfortable ignorance, you know where to find me.
— E.


“I will finish the sentence she wouldn’t.”
He did. Theron did too, tonight.
The Chancellor chose not to know. Two men chose not to say. Everyone was waiting for someone else to go first. That was the party.




The Three Parchment Slips — give all three simultaneously, Scene 2

Theron removes these from his locked desk drawer after the combat. Set them on the table. Hand this page to players — they work on it directly. Do not read them aloud sequentially; let players see all three at once.

SLIP ONE
The parchment is small, folded so many times the creases are deep as scars.

The Dawnmark rises when the anchor holds. The vessel must be willing. The energy of the third circuit does not disperse; it dwells.


SLIP TWO
Same hand as Slip One. Slightly different ink — written at a different time.

Ask the archivist what lives within the amber light. The answer is not in the records. Within them is the truth of the ritual’s end.


SLIP THREE
The handwriting matches but the parchment feels marginally different — recopied at some point.

Every third scholar agreed: the Dawnborn are the mechanism. The energy lives in willing vessels. The ritual them waits still.



The pattern: read every third word across all three slips in sequence.
Answer: THE DAWNBORN ARE THE VESSEL THE ENERGY LIVES WITHIN THEM
Theron encoded this for himself, not against the players. The real question is why someone would write a secret in a form designed to be found.
Slip Three was recopied — a player who examines it closely (DC 15 Insight) notices very slightly different ink. Theron went back and corrected a transcription error three years ago. He did not examine why he did that.

Theron knows all three names. He has never spoken them to the box. This is not because he forgot.

Corven’s Ritual Redirection Notes — from the Resonance Box

Hand this after the Resonance Box is opened successfully. This is in Corven’s handwriting — the same hand as the colophon, the same hand as the notation key. Four pages. The passage below is from the third page.

[The handwriting is steady for the first two pages. On the third page it changes — smaller, more compressed, as if he knew he was running out of room or time.]

The anchors are not lost. The light did not die. It redistributed into ten living vessels born at the moment of inversion. The ritual is incomplete, not failed. The completion requires their release.

[Below this, in the margin, the same hand, different ink — added later:]

The mechanism will not function as designed if the distinction is collapsed. Willing release is not the same mechanism as forced release. This is not a philosophical observation. It is an engineering specification.

[The fourth page is blank except for a single line at the bottom:]

No one should be forced.


“Their release.” The technical term Theron uses when he explains what this means is: extinguished.
Corven wrote the consent clause into the ritual because he understood it was load-bearing, not decorative. The ritual does not function the same way with unwilling anchors. The Reckoning either does not know this or has decided it does not matter.
The fourth page’s final line was added at a different time. It is in the same hand but the ink has aged differently — written years after the ritual, when Corven was still alive and still thinking about what he had built.

Tomas — The Long Preparation [player of Tomas’s closest PC only]

Play this when Tomas arrives mid-revelation at the Dawnhalls.

He reads the room before he reaches you. You can see him doing it — the way someone reads a situation who has been expecting this situation for a long time.
He sits down. He asks three questions. Each one is precise. Each one suggests he already knows the general shape of the answer and is confirming the details.
After the third question, he is quiet for a moment.
Then: “I saw a secondary notation in a ritual diagram once. About seven years ago — a copy of a copy, badly transcribed. I didn’t know what I was reading at the time. I filed it as ‘notation anomaly, unclear.’ I looked for the original twice. Never found it.”
He looks at the diagram in your hands.
“I think I found it now.”
He does not look afraid. He looks like someone who has been carrying a low-grade dread for a very long time and has just been told the thing he was dreading is real. That is, in a specific way, a relief.
What do you say to him?



Lira — The Hard No [player of Lira’s closest PC only]

Play this at the branching point, when Lira is told.

She goes still first. Not cold — still. The way someone goes still when they need a moment before they respond because the response that is coming without the moment would be the wrong one.
Then: “No.”
She looks around the room. At Sera. At Petra. At the wall.
“Find another way.”
She walks out.
She is not finished with this conversation. She is finished with it right now, in this room, with these people, while she is still deciding whether to trust any of you. She has a daughter the party may not know about yet. She has been saying no to the city’s needs since she was nineteen years old and her name started appearing on Dawnborn registry documents.
She will come back. She will want to know if there is actually another way.
If someone follows her: she stops walking. She doesn’t turn around. She says: “Give me an hour. If you have found an alternative, it will still be true in an hour.”
Do you follow her?



Kaelen — Reading the Reckoning [Moustaffa only]

Play this during either combat — Archive or Dawnhalls. No roll required.

You’ve fought organised units before. You know the difference between zealots and soldiers.
The Reckoning fights like soldiers.
Not fanatically. Not sacrificially. They have assigned roles — one to restrain, one to strike, one to control the exit. They have a priority hierarchy: documents first, Theron second, the party third. When Marsh takes a hit he doesn’t react emotionally. He recalculates.
These people have been training for this specific operation. Someone drilled them on the Archive layout. Someone told them where the restricted section was and what was in it.
The Reckoning isn’t a cult running on ideology. It’s a paramilitary unit running on an objective.
Who gave them the objective? Who funded the training?
You don’t have an answer. But you know what a well-resourced military unit looks like. This is one.

title: 26  Session 3 — The Watched City (Level 5)

Core reveals
Ellan Voss is alive. Her consent is withheld. She is Iza’s mother. The Concordance decoded the ritual diagram before the players did.


Three clue paths to Ellan
① Decoder + Fragment 3 → journal → address · ② Osindra: has observed the Concordance watching an Ashring street for three years · ③ Sera + legwork: DC 14 Investigation narrows to three houses

NPC
Where
Goal this session




Osindra

Trade intelligence; decide privately about the Concordance offer

Ironbell tannery, back wall, crossbow
Stay alive; give players two days of intelligence

Dusk Priest

The Watcher
Bound to Sending signature

Ellan Voss
Ashring, third lane, no knocker
Wait. She has been waiting for a very long time.







📁 Scene 1 — RP: The Divination Tower



📄 Five Senses & Arrival

Five senses: - Sight: A tower narrower than expected, no signage, windows filled with slowly rotating orreries that don’t match any charted sky. A brass speaking tube by the door, polished to a mirror finish. - Sound: Faint mechanical ticking from somewhere high above. Pages turning, though no one is visible through the windows. - Smell: Old ink and something sharper — ozone, like lightning held still. Faintly: tea, recently brewed. Exactly enough cups. - Touch: The door handle is warm, as if someone just let go of it. - Air: Still. The tower seems to be holding its breath.
The Prescience Door — mechanic for Sephandrius:
Before anyone can knock, the speaking tube crackles. A young apprentice’s voice, slightly out of breath: “We’ve been expecting you. All of you. The Divination Tower has three rules for visitors: no uninvited scrying past the second floor, no astral projection above the fourth, and—” sound of shuffling papers “—Sephandrius, your paper on temporal recursion was cited incorrectly in the Aldshire Compendium. Third footnote. Magistra Osindra would like to discuss that separately.”
The door opens before anyone touches it.
Inside, a teenage apprentice looks up from a desk covered in observation logs: “She’s been watching your approach for forty minutes. She says to tell you she saw the beacon go off, she’s cross about it, and to please wipe your feet.”
The apprentice’s notes, if players glance at them: a detailed log of their journey across the city — including “Sephandrius paused twice to adjust appearance before arrival. Noted.”



📄 Osindra — NPC

Magistra Vell Osindra — Divination Tower Master

Want: Remain neutral. She trades in information; sides are overhead costs she’d rather avoid.
Fear: The Concordance has a seer of their own — and she suspects theirs may be more accurate than hers.
Lie: She has already received an approach from the Concordance. An offer. She has not refused it. She is deciding between sessions.

Voice: Quiet, precise, never repeats herself. Addresses the group as “investigators.” Addresses Sephandrius by first name, as if they’ve argued before.
She doesn’t look up from the shallow basin of black water when they enter: “The beacon lit four scrying pools simultaneously. Whatever was in that room — three parties now have your description. Sit down.”
Osindra and Sephandrius: She knows his published work and has opinions. If it becomes clear Sephandrius is a diviner, she actually looks at him: “You’re better suited for this than I’d like you to be. Don’t let it go to your head.” On her neutrality: “I’m not neutral. I’m careful. There’s a difference.”
Intelligence she offers freely (she wants them moving before anyone connects the party to her tower): 1. The Concordance has operated in Varenhold for at least twenty years. Not improvised. 2. Their seer reads through resonance, not line-of-sight. Every spell cast in the open leaves an arcane signature — a footprint readable in real time. 3. “The Ironbell district has a dead zone for scrying — old clay pipes in the walls, copper-lined. Use them.”
What she doesn’t say: She knows the Concordance leadership’s name. The offer they made her includes information she doesn’t have yet.
GM Note — Session 4 betrayal hook: Decide before Session 4 whether Osindra accepts the offer. If yes, Session 4 can open with the party discovering their movements after this session were leaked.
Scene ends when she says, without looking up: “I’d appreciate it if no one saw you leave.”



📄 The Sending + GM Notes

Sending to Sera:
Osindra offers the tower’s amplified sending focus — a silver rod mounted in a resonance ring. With it, Sera’s response arrives clean. Without it: 50% chance one word is replaced by static.
Sera’s 25-word response:

“They knew my name before the beacon. Ironbell tannery, third lane. Come quiet. No magic in the streets — they have a seer. Maerin’s already coming.”

GM Note — “Maerin’s already coming”: Maerin Voss is a priest the players met in Session 0.5. Same surname as Sera — she is family. She heard two days ago that Sera had gone dark. She’s been moving toward Ironbell on her own.
GM Note — “They knew my name before the beacon”: Deliberate unsolved mystery. Do not resolve in Session 3. If players press Sera later, she doesn’t know how they identified her either.
GM Note — The Sending triggers The Watcher: The arcane signature of a Sending spell is large, clean, and distinctive. The Concordance seer reads it immediately. The Watcher — bound to track Sending signatures — is dispatched within minutes. It cannot enter the copper-pipe dead zone. It will be waiting.





📁 Scene 2 — Skill Challenge: Through the Watched Streets



📄 Five Senses & Setup

Five senses (Ironbell approach): - Sight: Narrower streets than the civic quarter — buildings lean together overhead, closing the sky to a grey strip. Loading docks, a tanner’s market with hanging hides, a water channel close to the wall. People who don’t make eye contact. - Sound: Iron bells, distant and irregular. Underfoot: cobbles give way to fitted stone over the copper-pipe infrastructure — a different sound when you tap it. - Smell: Tanning chemicals from three directions. Oak bark. Something biological and old. - Touch: The walls here are cooler than the open streets. The copper pipes behind the plaster radiate a faint chill. - The dead zone: When players enter the copper-pipe alley, every spellcaster feels a sudden silence — the arcane signature doesn’t propagate outward. Like casting into a room with no echo. It’s oddly peaceful.
The threat: The Concordance seer reads arcane signatures in real time. Operatives are positioned at key intersections. And at the edge of the copper-pipe zone: a shape that isn’t moving with the crowd. The Watcher is here.



📄 Challenge Table + Consequences

Stakes: 3 successes before 2 failures. Track failures silently — announce only what players can observe.









Roll

What it represents




Spot the watcher

Identify which figure is reading them, not just standing

No spells in the open streets. Each spell cast outside the copper-pipe zone grants the Concordance seer a position fix. Additionally, The Watcher moves 30 ft toward any arcane source as a free action. Casting during the skill challenge = automatic 1 failure, no roll.
Outcome tiers:







Result
What happens




Full success (3/0): Arrive clean.
Surprise round. Sera has had time to prepare a position. The Returned start clustered.


Partial (3/1): Tailed once.
No surprise. The Watcher is at the tannery perimeter — visible through shutter cracks. Watching.


Hard partial (3/2): Tailed and flagged.
No surprise. The Watcher enters through the lane-threshold gap at the start of Round 1. Reinforcement (1 additional Ghast) arrives end of Round 2 via the shuttered east window.


Full failure (2 failures before 3 successes): Seer locks on before they reach Ironbell.
Sera is captured before they arrive. Chase / rescue scenario replaces the combat. Session path changes significantly — see GM note below.



GM Note — Full failure: Players arrive at the tannery to find a fight has already ended. Sera is gone. One unconscious Unlit is left behind (extraction team moved fast). Run a chase through the copper-pipe district — Sera must be found before they move her out. Players can still reach Scene 4 and 5 through the rescued-Sera path. This is harder and darker, but survivable.



📄 The Watcher — First Appearance

At the edge of the copper-pipe zone, Passive Perception 14+: a shape at the alley mouth that doesn’t move like people move. It stands exactly at the boundary and does not cross it. When someone looks directly at it: it’s there. When they look again: it has shifted position, but is still at the boundary. Still watching.
If players approach: it retreats exactly as fast as they advance.
What players can learn (Arcana DC 13): Undead. Bound to something — not autonomous. Keyed to a specific arcane signature. Destroying it will not end the binding; it will re-manifest.
Full mechanics: In Scene 3 section.





📁 Scene 3 — Combat: The Tannery Ambush



📄 Five Senses & Setup

Five senses: - Sight: The tannery is shut. Shutters cracked. One amber lamp visible inside. Three figures in the lane — too still, too positioned. Their wrists glow faint violet. They are not alive. - Sound: The tanning chemicals hit before the building does. Under that: silence. The figures in the lane make no sound at all. Iron bells in the distance. - Touch: The lane cobbles are damp. The door has been opened recently — dust disturbed in a specific arc. - The uncanny: One figure’s wrist has a sealed-door brand, glowing softly. No breath vapour. They have been standing here for a long time.
Sera Voss is inside, crossbow across her knees, sitting against the far wall. Not frightened. Waiting. When she sees them: “Took longer than I expected.”
She has two days of intelligence to give. She doesn’t get the chance.
The ambush hits when players enter or signal entry. The three figures in the lane move simultaneously — coordinated, not hurried. The door behind the players closes. Two more were already inside.
Secondary Objective (state before first initiative roll): The Priest’s goal is to extract Sera alive. Players must fight and protect Sera simultaneously. If Sera drops to 0 HP (captured via Hold Person + drag), the Priest signals withdrawal — Session 4 changes significantly.
GM Note — If Sera is captured: Session 4 opens with the party needing to locate where she is held before pursuing Ellan Voss. The Concordance will attempt to use Sera — a willing Dawnborn — as leverage. This is a harder, darker path.



📄 Tannery Environment

Approximately 40 ft × 30 ft. Low ceiling. One amber lamp — the only light source.

Tanning vats ×3 (3 ft deep, acid/chemical solution): Creatures pushed in take 2d6 acid damage per turn; climbing out costs full movement. Shove available to adjacent creatures.
Hanging hides on wooden racks: Soft cover (−2 to ranged attacks through them). Difficult terrain. Athletics DC 11 to pull down — creates 10-ft area of difficult terrain.
The amber lamp (only light source): Smashing it (AC 10) plunges the tannery into darkness. The Returned and the Priest operate freely in darkness; players without darkvision are blinded. Dangerous.
Barrels of tanbark: Athletics DC 13 as a bonus action to push 10 ft — can block doorways or pin creatures.
Copper-pipe infrastructure: The tannery itself is inside the dead zone. The Watcher cannot enter through the walls. If players move into the lane during combat, The Watcher is there.

The Stench: The tannery’s chemical smell is extreme. At the start of combat, all creatures within the tannery must make an initial DC 11 CON save or be Poisoned for the first round. The Returned are immune. This is separate from the Ghasts’ own Stench ability.



📄 The Returned (Ghasts) × 3

Former Concordance initiates who died in service and were Returned by the Priest. The sealed-door brand glows faint violet on each wrist — evidence of the Priest’s work. They do not speak. They do not retreat without his signal. When they fall, they fall cleanly and silently. This is more unsettling than screaming.

Damage Immunities: Poison.
Condition Immunities: Charmed, exhaustion, poisoned.
Senses: Darkvision 60 ft. Passive Perception 10.

Special Traits
Stench. Any creature (other than undead) that starts its turn within 5 ft of a Returned must succeed on a DC 13 CON save or be Poisoned until the start of its next turn. On a successful save, the creature is immune to this Returned’s Stench for 24 hours. In the tannery, already full of chemical smell: players have disadvantage on this save for the first two rounds.
Pack Tactics. The Returned has advantage on attack rolls against a creature if at least one of its allies is within 5 ft of the creature and that ally isn’t incapacitated.

Actions
Claws. Melee Weapon Attack: +5 to hit, reach 5 ft, one target. Hit: 2d6+3 slashing. The target must succeed on a DC 13 CON save or be Paralyzed for 1 minute. A Paralyzed target can repeat the save at the end of each of its turns, ending the effect on a success. Undead are immune.
Bite. Melee Weapon Attack: +3 to hit, reach 5 ft, one creature that is Paralyzed. Hit: 3d6+3 piercing.

Tactics: The Returned operate to lock down players — Paralysis from Claws is their primary weapon. They use Pack Tactics wherever possible, staying adjacent to each other and adjacent to targets. Two prioritise players engaging the Priest. One positions between the party and Sera. They will not break formation to pursue retreating players — they hold their defensive positions. When the Priest signals withdrawal with the sealed-door hand gesture, all disengage simultaneously and exit through the lane door.
Note on Paralysis: A Paralyzed player is automatically hit by subsequent attacks, including Bite (which deals serious damage). This is the primary threat — the combination of Pack Tactics advantage + Paralysis + Bite can drop a character in two rounds. Players need to break up their clustering and prioritise saving Paralyzed allies.



📄 Dusk Priest (×1)

The Priest is controlled and efficient. He has done this before. He is visibly not quite right — too still between actions, eyes that track without blinking, breath that doesn’t cloud in the cool air. He is not undead. He has been in proximity to undead energy long enough that the distinction has blurred.
Identifying detail: A brass ring on his right hand, set with a fragment of black glass. He never removes it. Players who see it clearly and describe it to Theron or Osindra later: Theron identifies it as a senior Concordance leadership token. This pays off in a later session.

Saves: Wisdom +7, Charisma +5, Constitution +6.
Skills: Deception +5, Insight +7, Perception +7, Stealth +5.
Damage Resistances: Necrotic.
Senses: Darkvision 120 ft. Passive Perception 17.
Spellcasting. 9th-level spellcaster. Spellcasting ability Wisdom (spell save DC 15, +7 to hit).







Slots
Spells




At will
Toll the Dead (2d8; 2d12 if target missing HP), Thaumaturgy, Chill Touch


1st (4 slots)

Actions
Toll the Dead (cantrip). One target within 60 ft. WIS save DC 15. Fail: 2d8 necrotic (2d12 if below max HP). No concentration, no slot.
Inflict Wounds (1st-level slot). Melee Spell Attack: +7 to hit, reach 5 ft. Hit: 3d10 necrotic. Upcast to 3rd: 5d10.
Blight (4th-level slot). One target within 30 ft. CON save DC 15. Fail: 8d8 necrotic. Success: half.
Bonus Actions
Shadow Step. When in dim light or darkness: teleport up to 30 ft to another space in dim light or darkness. No opportunity attacks. Once per turn.
Spiritual Weapon (2nd-level slot, concentration-free). A spectral mace shaped like the sealed-door symbol appears. Bonus action to move and attack (+7 to hit, 1d8+4 force). Persists 1 minute.

Tactical Priority:
Round 1: Cast Darkness centred on the amber lamp — 15-ft radius of magical darkness. The Priest and The Returned see normally inside it. Players without Devil’s Sight or Truesight cannot see into the sphere and have disadvantage on attacks against targets inside. Sera is inside the zone.
If Darkness is Counterspelled: Spiritual Weapon + Toll the Dead. Shadow Step to a dim corner. Plan shifts to aggression.
Round 2: Hold Person targeting Sera (WIS save DC 15). If she fails: two Returned immediately move to drag her (10 ft per round). If she succeeds: Toll the Dead on the highest-HP visible player.
Round 3+: If Sera is being dragged: Shadow Step to block players pursuing the extraction. If Sera is free: repeat Hold Person (uses 2nd slot). If both 2nd slots spent: Blight on the most damaged player. Spiritual Weapon maintained throughout.
Withdrawal trigger: 2 of 3 Returned downed, OR the Priest drops below 30 HP. He makes the sealed-door hand gesture. All remaining Returned disengage simultaneously. Priest casts Misty Step to exit, then Dashes. They do not fight to the death.
Bestow Curse / Shadow of Moil: Only if combat extends past 5 rounds. Bestow Curse on the most active player (disadvantage on WIS saves — makes Hold Person harder to resist). Shadow of Moil is last resort: 4d12 necrotic per turn to adjacent attackers, heavily obscures the Priest.



📄 The Watcher (Revenant) — Persistent Threat

Bound to the arcane trace of the Sending spell. Not autonomous — directed. It cannot think, cannot feel, cannot be reasoned with. It was someone once. The Concordance does not consider this a tragedy.
The Watcher cannot enter the copper-pipe dead zone… unless there is a gap. The lane-side entrance to the tannery has a brief exposed section in the copper-pipe network. On specific skill challenge outcomes, this gap is enough.



Type
Undead (Revenant, modified)


CR
5
